To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ventilation of the lungs with any gas mixture during ischemia prevents reperfusion injury.
lung inflation and instillation of surfactant before ischemia prevent reperfusion injury in the isolated-perfussed rat lung model.
ventilation of the lungs by 20% O2 or 100% nitrogen and supplementation of surfantant prevent reperfuion-induced lung microvascular damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of lung reperfusion injury, which is a major problem in lung transplantation.
the mechanisms of postreper fusion lung injury.
the role of surfactant and ventilation in preventing reperfusion-induced microvascular injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the state of the lung during ischemia is a key factor in the development of lung injury.
ventilation of the lung during ischemia prevents microvascular injury during the reflow period, and that surfactant pretreatment of the collapsed lung prevents the development of vascular injury.
the state of pulmonary inflation during ischemia is an important determinant in the development of lung microvascular injury during reperusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the state of the alveolar-capillary barrier during ischemia contributes substantially to the extent of reperfusion-induced injury.
lung ventilation and surfactants are protective against reperfusion injury in the lung.
lung inflation and/or surfactant pretreatment before ischemia may be beneficial in preventing reperfusion-induced vascular injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state of pulmonary inflation during ischemia plays a major role in the development of reperfusion-induced vascular injury.
ventilation and surfactants can be used to prevent lung microvascular injury.
the state of inflation of the lung during ischemia is an important determinant of lung reperfusion-induced vascular injury and that surfactant pretreatment can prevent this injury.
